Source: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, Commodity Price Data (The
Pink Sheet), `CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx`, release of 2026-09-02,
downloaded 2026-10-10 (`_data/raw/worldbank/`), sheet Annual Prices (Real),
2010 US dollars deflated by the MUV index.
Pipeline script: `_scripts/03-controls-prices.R` (weights from
`03-controls-agro.R`).
Interim outputs: `_data/interim/prices_real_normalized_2000_2020.rds`,
`prices_index_2000_2020.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 03 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
pink_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/worldbank/CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx",
                       sheet = "Annual Prices (Real)", col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
                       .name_repair = "minimal")
prices_norm <- read_rds("_data/interim/prices_real_normalized_2000_2020.rds")
prices_index <- read_rds("_data/interim/prices_index_2000_2020.rds")
weights <- read_rds("_data/interim/pam_ppm_weights_base_2000_2002.rds")
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
```

## Q1. What is the layout and the release of the workbook?

```{r q1-layout}
excel_sheets("_data/raw/worldbank/CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx")
pink_raw[1:4, 1]
series <- c("Soybeans", "Maize", "Rice, Thai 5%", "Cotton, A Index", "Beef")
idx <- match(series, str_trim(unlist(pink_raw[7, ])))
tibble(series, column = idx, unit = str_trim(unlist(pink_raw[8, idx])),
       first_year = pink_raw[[1]][9], last_year = pink_raw[[1]][nrow(pink_raw)])
```

**Finding.** The sheet keeps the legacy layout: commodity names on row 7,
units on row 8, data from row 9 (1960) to 2025, year in the first column.
The release header reads "Updated on September 02, 2026". The five series
are present under their legacy names, soy, maize and rice in dollars per
tonne, cotton and beef per kilogram.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-a (release accepted; the real series are
recomputed at each MUV revision, so the indices drift from the lost
release by a fraction of a percent).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, raw-state block (names, units,
first year, complete 2000-2020).

## Q2. How do the normalised real series move over 2000-2020?

```{r q2-plot}
#| fig-height: 4
prices_norm %>%
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "commodity", values_to = "index") %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, index, colour = commodity)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Real price, 2000 = 1", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
prices_norm %>% filter(year %in% c(2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020))
```

**Finding.** All five series equal 1 in 2000 by construction; rice peaks
at 2.5 in 2008, maize at 2.4 and soy at 2.0 in 2012, cotton at 1.8 in
2011 before returning to its base, and beef climbs steadily to twice its
2000 level by 2019-2020.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-h.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, output block (2000 values equal 1,
positive series).

## Q3. Is the index anchored to 1 in 2000 for both crop and cattle?

```{r q3-anchor}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, year == 2000) %>%
  summarise(across(c(price_index_crop, price_index_cattle),
                   list(n_na = ~ sum(is.na(.x)), min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        p50 = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("index", "stat"),
               names_pattern = "(price_index_[a-z]+)_(n_na|min|p50|max)$") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
prices_index %>% filter(geocode == "1100015", year %in% 2000:2002) %>%
  left_join(weights, by = "geocode") %>%
  select(year, price_index_crop, price_index_cattle, cattle_weight)
```

**Finding.** Neither index is 1 in 2000. The crop index in 2000 equals the
municipality's total base-window crop share (a few hundredths for most of
the sample) and the cattle index equals its base-window density (tens of
heads per km2), because the weights do not sum to one and normalisation
ran before the join.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-p (open, phase 2 step 2.4; task 1.3). Reproduced
on purpose.
**Assertion.** none in phase 1 (KNOWN DEFECTS block).

## Q4. Are the scales comparable?

```{r q4-scales}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("price_index"), names_to = "index", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(index) %>%
  summarise(n_na = sum(is.na(value)), min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE), p50 = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** The cattle index is three orders of magnitude larger than the
crop index and both carry the cross-sectional scale of the weights, so a
pooled coefficient is not interpretable; script 04 standardises them and
phase 2 re-anchors them.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-p (open).

## Q5. Which municipalities have a zero or missing index, and why?

```{r q5-missing}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, year == 2000,
         is.na(price_index_crop) | price_index_crop == 0 | is.na(price_index_cattle)) %>%
  left_join(weights, by = "geocode") %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, price_index_crop, price_index_cattle,
         starts_with("crop_w_"), cattle_weight)
```

**Finding.** Nine sample municipalities have a zero or missing index in
2000. Five (Barcelos, Santa Isabel do Rio Negro and Uarini in Amazonas,
Belém and Marituba in Pará) planted none of the four crops in 2000-2002,
so their crop index is a true zero. Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá and Mojuí
dos Campos have a crop index of 0 because their four weights are NA (no
PAM value in the window) and the weighted sum drops NA terms, and no
cattle index, their density weight being NA. Santa Cruz do Arari has no
crop index, having no PAM series, and keeps its cattle index through the
full join of the two indices.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-h (zero for an all-NA window, inherited);
D-2026-10-10-i (Santa Cruz do Arari); task 1.8 for the coding of absence.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, output block (crop index NA exactly
for municipalities without a PAM series; lag NA in 2000 or where the index
is NA).
